paragraphs: R’ Levi Tzanavriya. (The name of a city, as in Megillah, chapter 3, halakhah 1.)

He is mentioned in Sheviit, chapter 6, halakhah 2, where he asked R’ Yitzchak and R’ Immi; and there, chapter 9, halakhah 5, he asked R’ Ba bar Zavda (the Zhitomir printing has simply “R’ Levi”). In Avodah Zarah, end of chapter 2: “Levi Tzanavriya’s servant boy was selling produce” [the matching passage; supplied מלויא … מוכן differs]. Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha reports in Rabbi Yasa’s name: “The servant of a trustworthy person is like the trustworthy person.” Hyman explains: his young men were selling produce under the presumption that it had been tithed. Avodah Zarah 39a brings something similar about R’ Levi’s servant; see his entry.

notes.text: The supplied preparing-produce phrase and מלויא remain difficult; Hyman’s own gloss says that the attendants sold produce presumed tithed. No silent correction to selling is adopted. The requested end-of-chapter passage was unavailable.

The whole saved Venice Avodah Zarah2 scalar, indices8/6, actually contains טלייא דלוי צנבריא הוה מזבן פירין, Levi Tzanavriya’s servant boy selling produce, followed by Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha in Rabbi Yasa’s name and the trustworthy-servant rule. This withdraws the older blanket passage-unavailable claim. Supplied מלויא and מוכן remain explicit beside the matching reading, not proved printing/transcription errors. Hyman’s own young-men-selling gloss is distinguished from the literal preparing reading. The exact quoted Levi has no full title, so no Rabbi is transferred to the heading, Sheviit or Zhitomir occurrences. Named Yaakov/Yasa full titles are local to the inspected clause. All locators and separate Bavli servant pointer remain, no identity merge.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 864) reads טלייא, a boy, where the supplied Hebrew has מלויא, and it also reads מוכן where the consulted Venice Yerushalmi has מזבן, selling. Hyman’s own gloss says the young men sold produce presumed tithed. Both consulted Sheviit passages name Levi with the place epithet and give the same questioned sages as Hyman. Megillah 3:1 mentions the Torah scroll of the people of Tzanavriya in the Ursicinus episode. The Zhitomir reading remains Hyman’s report. In the Bavli’s example at Avodah Zarah 39a, the servant used to sell asafoetida, and those who consulted Rabbi Yochanan asked whether they could still buy from him after Rabbi Levi’s death. The parallel does not establish a shared identity.
